results.name: Dumbbell Decline Triceps Pull-Over Extension
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your feet secured and hold a dumbbell with both hands, extending your arms straight above your chest.
Slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head, keeping your arms slightly bent at the elbows.
Once your arms are almost parallel to the floor, bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells down to your head sides, and immediately straighten your elbows.
Raise both dumbbells in an arc over your head to starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid locking your elbows; maintain a slight bend to reduce joint strain.
Perform the movement slowly to maximize muscle activation and control.
Ensure a full range of motion for optimal muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell Decline Triceps Pull-Over Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Incline Triceps Extension
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and lie back against it. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended straight up, palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells behind your head in a controlled motion.
Lower the dumbbells until your forearms are parallel to the floor, maintaining a 90-degree angle at your elbows.
Extend your elbows to raise the dumbbells back to the starting position, keeping your upper arms stationary. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you extend the dumbbells upward and inhale as you lower them.
Keep your upper arms stationary to ensure the movement targets your triceps.
Use a slow and controlled motion to avoid swinging and ensure proper muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell Incline Triceps Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Incline Two Arm Extension
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and lie back against it, holding a single dumbbell with both hands, gripping the handle securely. Start with the dumbbell extended straight up above your shoulders, with your palms facing each other.
Slowly lower the dumbbell by bending your elbows, allowing the weight to move behind your head until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom of the movement, feeling the stretch in your triceps.
Reverse the motion by extending your elbows, pushing the dumbbell back up to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement to maintain tension on the muscles.
Exhale as you extend the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
Use a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement and reduce the risk of injury.
results.description: Dumbbell Incline Two Arm Extension is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Kickback
instructions: Begin by kneeling with the right leg on a bench and the left foot firmly planted on the floor. Lean down until your torso is parallel to the floor and place your right hand on the bench for support.Hold a dumbbell in the right hand.
Start with your right arm bent at a 90-degree angle, with the upper arm parallel to the floor and the dumbbell close to your torso.
Extend your arm backward by straightening your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary and focusing on squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.

Slowly bend your elbow to return to the starting position, maintaining control and keeping your upper arm parallel to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching to the other arm.
tips: Keep your upper arm stationary throughout the movement to isolate the triceps effectively.
Engage your core to maintain stability and prevent excessive movement of your torso.
Use a controlled motion, avoiding swinging the dumbbell to ensure proper muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell Kickback is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Neutral Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on your back on a flat bench with your feet firmly planted on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in one hand with a neutral grip, arm bent so that the forearm is parallel to the floor. Use your free hand to support the elbow of the working arm.
Keeping your upper arm stationary, extend your elbow to lift the dumbbell towards the ceiling.

Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control, ensuring your forearm returns to being parallel to the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Avoid locking your elbow at the top of the movement to prevent joint strain.
Focus on a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.
Exhale as you extend your arm and inhale as you lower the dumbbell.
results.description: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Neutral Triceps Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension on Floor
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, arms extended towards the ceiling, and palms facing each other. Position the dumbbell directly above your chest with your elbows slightly bent.
Slowly bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell towards the floor just behind your forehead, keeping your upper arms stationary and elbows pointing towards the ceiling.
Extend your elbows to raise the dumbbell back towards the ceiling until your arms are fully extended, keeping your upper arms stationary throughout the movement.
Repeat the movements for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to ensure maximum triceps engagement.
Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled motion.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain and injuries.
results.description: Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension on Floor is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and knees bent at a 90-degree angle. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms bent and forearms parallel to the floor, palms facing each other.
Keeping your elbows stable, slowly extend your elbows to raise the dumbbells towards the ceiling until your arms are fully extended, keeping your upper arms stationary.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position by bending your elbows, ensuring your forearms return to being parallel to the floor.
Repeat the movements for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control and proper form throughout the exercise.
tips: Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms to ensure maximum triceps engagement.
Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled motion throughout the exercise.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain and injuries.
results.description: Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Kickback
instructions: Start in a semi-lunge position with your left foot firmly planted on the floor in front and your right leg extended behind you lightly bent on your forefoot. Lean forward and place your left arm on your left knee for support.
Hold a dumbbell in your right hand with your arm bent at a 90-degree angle, keeping your upper arm close to your torso and parallel to the floor and your forearm pointing back.
Extend your elbow to straighten your arm, moving the dumbbell backward until your arm is fully extended.
Slowly bend your elbow to return the dumbbell to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Keep your upper arm stationary throughout the exercise to isolate the triceps.
Perform the movement in a slow and controlled manner to maximize muscle engagement.
Avoid swinging the dumbbell or using momentum to lift the weight.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Kickback is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell One Arm Triceps Extension (On Bench)
instructions: Begin by sitting on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand, extending your arm straight above your shoulder. Place your left hand on your hip for support.
Lower the dumbbell slowly behind your head by bending your elbow, keeping your upper arm stationary and your wrist straight.
Extend your arm back to the starting position, fully straightening your elbow and squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid flaring your elbow out to the side; keep it close to your head.
Focus on isolating the triceps muscle by keeping your upper arm still.
Exhale as you extend your arm and inhale as you lower the dumbbell.
results.description: Dumbbell One Arm Triceps Extension (On Bench) is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Overhead Extension Seated
instructions: Sit on a bench, holding a dumbbell with both hands and extending your arms fully overhead. Hold a dumbbell with your fingers wrapped around the dumbbell handle.
Slowly bend your elbows, lowering the dumbbell behind your head until your forearms are parallel to the floor.
Press the dumbbell back up by straightening your elbows, returning to the starting position with arms fully extended overhead.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, keeping your core engaged and back pressed against the bench.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your head throughout the movement to maximize triceps activation.
Use a controlled motion, avoiding any jerking or swinging of the weight.
Maintain a firm grip on the dumbbell to ensure stability and control.
results.description: Dumbbell Overhead Extension Seated is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.
